bug_semantics: A FAQ editor can plant an whose src points at a local file under content/ (e.g. content/core/config/database.php). PDF export WriteHTML() reaches Wrapper::Image(), which file_get_contents()s that path and runs imagecreatefromstring/getimagesizefromstring. On non-image bytes those PHP warnings are promoted to ErrorException by the global error handler; the uncaught stack trace reflects a truncated (or, if zend.exception_string_param_max_len is raised, full) slice of the file, including credentials. CVE-2026-57961 only blocked traversal outside the web root; content/ remained readable.
flaw_origin: On 2024-11-08 Thorsten Rinne (06df60e7) rewrote Wrapper::Image() to load PMF_ROOT_DIR.$file via file_get_contents and validate with checkBase64Image() (imagecreatefromstring without swallowing warnings), then still called parent::Image(). Parent b1d25c3b only parse_url()d and delegated to TCPDF. Later 91ce6440/b709ebe6 restricted concatenatePaths to content/ and isWithinRoot (classic traversal), leaving the in-root leak. 4.1.7 7a82e3ff returns if checkBase64Image fails and swallows E_WARNING around image parsing.
ai_marker: absent; author Thorsten Rinne <thorsten@phpmyfaq.de>, committer Thorsten Rinne <thorsten@phpmyfaq.de>; cat-file -p shows only subject "fix: avoid image display errors in PDF due to SSL verification and caching issues" with no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, or bot identity
evidence: First-party GHSA-c63q-xx7x-j8w2 (bundle GHSA-m98p-5698-x2wc / CVE-2026-76210, withdrawn_at null): phpMyFAQ <4.1.7 PDF local file disclosure via img src under content/; patched 4.1.7. Clone phpmyfaq. Vulnerable path phpmyfaq/src/phpMyFAQ/Export/Pdf/Wrapper.php Image(): 4.1.6 does $data = file_get_contents($resolvedPath); if (checkBase64Image($data)) { $file = "@".$data; } then parent::Image($file) so non-images still reach TCPDF after imagecreatefromstring has already parsed the bytes. git log -S checkBase64Image on Wrapper.php first hits 06df60e776115aaeaeb99397330786cb89fcae63 adding $data = file_get_contents(PMF_ROOT_DIR . $file) plus checkBase64Image calling imagecreatefromstring without an error-handler. Parent b1d25c3bf793de015917b6653facb8eef2e2a772 Image() only handled data:image/png;base64, parse_url, parent::Image — no file_get_contents/checkBase64Image. Core/Error.php already threw ErrorException from the warning handler at that commit. 91ce64405479933d7d62c751fa79c2f5c6fda591 (cherry-picked b709ebe69405385785c2a74ae940c3e8d4cd0a8b) adds content/ + isWithinRoot (CVE-2026-57961 remainder). Direct fix 7a82e3ff591790a2f00a5fb4c7da861edaacde9b (parent 198fc0411c036e9dadf1ebd375ff5e873446b410) early-returns on failed checkBase64Image and set_error_handler swallows E_WARNING; tests assert probing a non-image under content/user/images does not leak. merge-base --is-ancestor BIC 4.1.6 yes; fix not ancestor of 4.1.6; fix ancestor of 4.1.7.
reasoning: The disclosure is not generic TCPDF HTML rendering; it is phpMyFAQ wrapping Image() so attacker-controlled content/ paths are file_get_contents()d and fed to GD, with warnings promoted to exceptions that echo the file. That sink first appears in single-parent 06df60e7; the parent tree lacks it. Hardening that limited paths to content/ is a different CWE-22 leftover, not this BIC. 7a82e3ff is the first content change that refuses non-image bytes and suppresses the leaking warning, landing in 4.1.7. BIC author/committer is Thorsten Rinne with no AI trailers or bot identity, so NOT_AI.
